# wso2is_oidc_scope (Resource)

Manages an OpenID Connect scope. When an application requests the scope, the server returns the scope's OIDC claims in ID tokens and from the `/userinfo` endpoint. The claims must exist in the `http://wso2.org/oidc/claim` dialect. You can also import and change the built-in scopes, such as `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `phone` and `address`. To import, use the scope name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom scope that releases contact details. Claims are OIDC claim names
# (external claims of the http://wso2.org/oidc/claim dialect).
resource "wso2is_oidc_scope" "contact" {
  name         = "contact"
  display_name = "Contact details"
  description  = "Email address and phone number"
  claims       = ["email", "phone_number"]
}

# Custom claims need an OIDC mapping first.
resource "wso2is_external_claim" "department" {
  dialect_uri            = "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim"
  claim_uri              = "department"
  mapped_local_claim_uri = "http://wso2.org/claims/department"
}

resource "wso2is_oidc_scope" "employment" {
  name         = "employment"
  display_name = "Employment details"
  claims       = [wso2is_external_claim.department.claim_uri]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Display name shown on consent pages.
- `name` (String) Scope name. Changing it replaces the scope.

### Optional

- `claims` (Set of String) OIDC claim names, for example `email`, `given_name`, or custom ones mapped with `wso2is_external_claim`.
- `description` (String) Description.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Scope name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_oidc_scope.employee employee
```
